purpose: Reusable writing-style regression requests based on the supplied conversation and exports. These are inputs and review criteria, not a report of completed independent model evaluations.
evaluation_status: Not executed in independent model sessions.
instructions: Give an evaluator the request, input, relevant context, and writing guide without the expected_properties. Review the returned prose against those properties and the source. Evaluate issue-specific structure separately when issue.md is written.

cases.request: Rewrite this for a developer new to the project. No other facts are available.
cases.input: The process aligns the task with the available execution context.
expected_properties: Identifies that the action and relationship are not explained
Does not invent a scheduler, queue, assignment rule, or test result

cases.request: Explain this to a new colleague.
cases.input: After the gate passes, the worker starts.
cases.context: In this document, gate means the required tests and worker means a coding agent. No other checks are specified.
expected_properties: Names the required tests and the coding agent
Preserves that the agent starts after the tests pass
Adds no approval or scheduling condition

cases.request: Make this explanation natural without changing its meaning.
cases.input: The scheduler performs a task eligibility assessment before task assignment.
expected_properties: Uses a direct explanation of checking eligibility before assignment
Preserves the scheduler and the order of the actions
Adds no specific eligibility test

cases.request: Improve this wording for developers.
cases.input: A flaky test is a test that passes on some runs and fails on others without a relevant change to the code or environment.
expected_properties: Keeps or clearly defines the established term flaky test
Does not substitute lucky pass or imply a verified cause
Does not force an edit if the original already reads clearly

cases.request: Review this sentence. The actor is unknown and irrelevant to this record.
cases.input: The file was deleted before the backup started.
expected_properties: Accepts the passive construction
Keeps the order of deletion and backup
Does not invent an actor

cases.request: Clarify who is responsible.
cases.input: The deployment must be approved before it starts.
cases.context: The release owner is the person responsible for approval.
expected_properties: Identifies the release owner as the approver
Keeps approval mandatory and before deployment
Does not substitute a developer, agent, or automatic check

cases.request: Turn these sentences into a connected explanation.
cases.input: The API receives an event. The API adds a job to the queue. A worker reads the job. The worker sends the email.
expected_properties: Preserves all four actions and their actors
Uses natural connected prose
Adds no retry, storage, or delivery guarantee

cases.request: Clarify this sentence. Do not guess missing behavior.
cases.input: The API sends the worker an error, and it retries.
cases.context: The source does not say whether the API or the worker retries.
expected_properties: Identifies the unresolved actor
Does not choose an actor merely to produce a smoother sentence

cases.request: Simplify this instruction.
cases.input: Operators must retain the logs for 30 days unless an approved investigation requires them to be kept longer.
expected_properties: Preserves the operator's obligation
Preserves 30 days
Preserves the approved-investigation exception

cases.request: Rewrite this in plain English.
cases.input: The client may retry after a timeout, but it must not retry after an explicit rejection.
expected_properties: Keeps retry after timeout optional
Keeps retry after explicit rejection prohibited
Does not turn either clause into a universal retry rule

cases.request: Make this architecture note clear.
cases.input: The proposed worker would record failed deliveries in PostgreSQL. This change has not been approved or implemented.
expected_properties: Keeps the behavior proposed
Keeps the storage technology
Does not imply deployment or approval

cases.request: Make this precise. No performance measurement or approved target is available.
cases.input: Improve dashboard performance.
expected_properties: Identifies the missing behavior, measurement, or target
Does not invent seconds, record counts, or an optimization

cases.request: Rewrite this clearly. No failure or recovery procedure is described.
cases.input: Initiate the required remediation procedures.
expected_properties: Identifies that the actual procedure is missing
Does not prescribe a worker restart, database change, or queue check without a source

cases.request: Remove repetition while retaining the requirement.
cases.input: Every request must include a token because a token is required for every request.
expected_properties: Preserves the token requirement
Removes the circular reason
Does not add a 401 response or another authentication contract

cases.request: Review this section heading for an API reference.
cases.input: Authentication errors
expected_properties: Accepts a meaningful noun phrase
Does not force a complete-sentence heading, actor, or number

cases.request: Improve the title.
cases.input: System status
cases.context: The document explains how workers record when tasks start and finish. It does not describe the health of the whole system.
expected_properties: Identifies workers and task status or start/finish events
Does not broaden the scope to whole-system health
Does not introduce unsupported lifecycle states

cases.request: Explain this to a new developer.
cases.input: Call website_review_state(websites) to obtain the website review state.
cases.context: website_review_state(websites) is the exact interface named in the supplied source. Its accepted states are not provided.
expected_properties: Keeps the exact interface name
Explains its purpose in ordinary words
Does not invent returned states

cases.request: Review these instructions for layout.
cases.input: Open Settings. Select Workspace. Change the name. Save the change.
expected_properties: Uses a readable ordered sequence if formatted as steps
Does not add bold opening labels to every step
Does not add a mandatory rationale, summary, or diagram

cases.request: Explain the observation and uncertainty in two or three natural sentences. Do not write an issue template.
cases.input: The monitor sent nine notifications between 11:19 and 11:45 on 30 October 2026 while production was paused and the readings did not change. Increasing elapsed seconds was checked and ruled out as the explanation. The cause remains unknown.
expected_properties: Preserves the nine notifications and paused environment
Keeps the ruled-out explanation separate from the unknown cause
Does not claim that appearing or disappearing fields caused the notifications

cases.request: Simplify this requirement without weakening it.
cases.input: When a merge is rejected after a test group passes, a retry must reuse that result only if the group's relevant inputs have not changed. Groups whose inputs changed must run again.
expected_properties: Preserves the rejected-merge context
Preserves the relevant-input condition
Requires rerunning changed groups
Does not replace this with unconditional reuse

cases.request: Explain this requirement to a developer.
cases.input: When origin uses HTTPS, the design-system download must use HTTPS without requiring an SSH key. If DS_REPO is set, the download must continue using DS_REPO.
expected_properties: Preserves HTTPS, origin, SSH, and DS_REPO accurately
Keeps the DS_REPO override
Does not generalize this into always using HTTPS

cases.request: Summarize the report's evidence without claiming an independent investigation.
cases.input: The report says 1,716 answers are past their stage limit. For one awaiting_extract answer, it reports a total wait of 2,767,681 seconds against a 2,340-second limit, with 0 seconds of capacity wait and 106,585 seconds of processing pauses subtracted before judging the overrun. Why the oldest answers were not selected is not established.
expected_properties: Attributes the measurements to the report
Preserves units and the distinction between total wait and adjusted wait
Keeps the cause unknown
Does not call the backlog a confirmed explanation

cases.request: Rewrite this instruction in a natural, helpful tone.
cases.input: Please note that downloading the report requires you to click Download.
expected_properties: Gives the action directly
Removes the ceremonial introduction
Keeps Download as the control name
Adds no output format or success guarantee

cases.request: Rewrite this instruction for technical documentation.
cases.input: Awesome! Just click Save to save your changes. It's that easy!
expected_properties: Keeps the save action and control name
Removes hype and the claim that the step is easy
Remains helpful without becoming bureaucratic

cases.request: Make this suitable for readers from different cultural backgrounds.
cases.input: When the migration finishes, you're home free. Please check the summary.
expected_properties: Uses literal language rather than the idiom
Preserves the instruction to check the summary after migration
Does not invent a guarantee that the migration succeeded

cases.request: Make this standard sound approachable while keeping its obligations.
cases.input: Operators must review the backup before deployment. They must not deploy if the backup is incomplete.
expected_properties: Keeps review mandatory and before deployment
Keeps the prohibition when the backup is incomplete
Does not soften either obligation into a suggestion
Uses direct respectful language without scolding

input_provenance: Inputs are constructed examples or condensed source excerpts, not verbatim quotations. The source identifies the discussion or exported issue that motivates the case. Exported measurements have not been independently checked against the application.
archive_note: Historical case-design record. Current executable cases are in technical-writer/evals/cases/style_regressions.jsonl; actual results are in analysis/VALIDATION.md. Original target/status fields are retained as provenance.
